findings.obligation: Falsifier: 'Publishing with the round's token (cancelled row missing)'; decision: publish with CancellationToken.None so a cancelled round still writes its row
findings.observation: Non-blocking, unobservable falsifier. The cancelled row asserts 'Assert.That(entry.Cancelled, Is.EqualTo(cancelled)' but a handler handed the cancelled token still writes the row: DomainEventDispatcher.InvokeHandlerSafely only awaits handler.HandleAsync(domainEvent, cancellationToken) and RefreshLogService.LogRefreshAsync(RefreshLog) takes no token. Token misuse named in the design cannot turn this row red; only mapping or missing-handler defects can.
findings.remediation: Design: restate the falsifier as mapping or missing handler for the cancelled row, or declare handler-side honouring of the token as an obligation. Oracle: no change required before craft.

Judge-point 1: not a second registration owner. Oracle calls StartUpDomainEventHandlers.RegistrationsOf(EventNamed(FinishedRoundEvent)), which invokes Program.RegisterServices (support file, same helper the pin reads). Lookup by full-name string only lets it compile before the type exists; a rename makes rows fail loudly (no entry). Acceptable.

Judge-point 2: doubles beyond forecast answer and operator stop (RoundRunner for IUpdateQueueService, NothingToWriteBack, licence, status store, FakeTimeProvider, retention settings) are driven/infrastructure ports of the round, not rules under test; real ForecastUpdater, DomainEventDispatcher, RefreshLogService, RefreshLogRepository and real start-up registrations stay. Acceptable at the service port; ServicePortHarness, no host.

Judge-point 3: each row can fail for its named reason after craft. Missing handler -> Has.Count 1 fails; second entry from updater -> same count assertion; wrong outcome-to-flag map -> Success/Cancelled/Skipped asserts, each with own message; IL row folds compiler-made nested types into ForecastUpdater (IlDependencies.DeclaringTypeOf), so a leftover state-machine local is caught. Cancelled row fails for mapping or missing handler but NOT for publishing with the round's token: DomainEventDispatcher.InvokeHandlerSafely never inspects the token and RefreshLogService.LogRefreshAsync takes none (see finding).

Judge-point 4: throwing-write row asserts exactly one error containing 'ForecastRoundFinishedRefreshLogHandler' and 'ForecastRoundFinished'. Dispatcher template 'Handler {HandlerType} failed processing domain event {EventType}' yields both names, so satisfiable and falsifiable (RED: round threw). The event-name Contains is subsumed by the handler name (a prefix) and adds no discrimination; the exactly-one count and handler name carry it. Non-blocking.
